pending_reasons.User has reached the per-user job slot l: Users are allowed 4 total cores. That can either be 1 4core session, 2 2core sessions, etc...

notes.memlimit_multiplier: Multiplier applied to memory_gb to calculate the -M (memory limit) value. The -R rusage[mem=] uses the base memory_gb value, while -M uses memory_gb * memlimit_multiplier. This allows setting a higher kill limit than the reservation. Example: memory_gb=16 with memlimit_multiplier=2.0 results in -R 'rusage[mem=16G]' -M 32G
notes.pending_reasons: Optional map of LSF pending reason text to a plain-language explanation of the local policy behind it. When a job is PEND, the UI hover tooltip shows the raw LSF reason plus this explanation when the LSF reason contains one of these keys (case-insensitive substring match). Reasons without a matching key show only the raw LSF text. May be given either as an object {reason: explanation} or as a list of such objects.
notes.queue_settings: Optional per-queue overrides. Maps a queue name (from available_queues) to a dict that overrides the global settings for that queue only. Supported keys: num_cores, memory_gb, os (per-queue defaults); memlimit_multiplier; memory_options_gb, enabled_memory_options_gb, core_options, enabled_core_options (per-queue option lists); and enabled_os_options (list of OS names, drawn from the global os_options). Any key that is omitted for a queue falls back to the global value, so configs without queue_settings behave exactly as before. enabled_* lists must be subsets of their corresponding available lists.
